decisive_items: 3-week history of worsening crampy abdominal pain
segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon
subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, mild crypt architectural distortion, and an acute inflammatory infiltrate without granulomas or dysplasia
response.rationale: Subacute bloody diarrhea, segmental left-sided colitis with rectal sparing, markedly elevated fecal calprotectin, and crypt architectural distortion favor inflammatory bowel disease over ischemic colitis. Ischemic colitis is less likely given the 3-week course, young age, and lack of acute vascular risk factors.

rejected.why: Ischemic colitis can produce left-colon ulceration and hemorrhage, but the subacute 3-week course and crypt architectural distortion favor IBD.
Diverticulitis is excluded by the explicit absence of diverticulosis and no perforation or abscess.
Clostridioides difficile infection is excluded by negative stool culture and toxin assays.
Microscopic colitis typically has normal-appearing mucosa and watery diarrhea, not segmental ulceration and bloody diarrhea.
Gastroenteritis is typically acute and self-limited; negative stool cultures and crypt architectural distortion argue against it.
Colitis is too nonspecific; the clinical, endoscopic, and histologic features are better explained by inflammatory bowel disease.
